claims.title: Portuguese navigators sight the islands
claims.summary: Vasco da Gama's second voyage to India recorded the Amirantes group; further Portuguese sightings followed in the early 1500s, giving Europe its first knowledge of the archipelago.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1502-portuguese-navigators-sight-the-islands, claim TL:SYC:event:1502:portuguese-navigators-sight-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First recorded landing by the Ascension
claims.summary: Crew of the English East India Company ship Ascension landed and found the islands fertile and uninhabited, but the Company chose not to settle.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1609-first-recorded-landing-by-the-ascension, claim TL:SYC:event:1609:first-recorded-landing-by-the-ascension, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A haunt of pirates
claims.summary: For a century and a half the empty islands were used by pirates as a hideout and watering place while they preyed on Indian Ocean shipping.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1700-a-haunt-of-pirates, claim TL:SYC:event:1700:a-haunt-of-pirates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France claims and names the islands
claims.summary: Corneille Nicholas Morphey laid a stone of possession and named the archipelago after finance minister Jean Moreau de Séchelles; the main island was named Mahé.

sources.label: The French History of the Seychelles

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1756-france-claims-and-names-the-islands, claim TL:SYC:event:1756:france-claims-and-names-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First permanent settlement
claims.summary: Colonists, enslaved Africans and Indians established the first lasting settlement near Mahé to begin spice cultivation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1770-first-permanent-settlement, claim TL:SYC:event:1770:first-permanent-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spice and plantation economy
claims.summary: Pierre Poivre promoted spice gardens to challenge the Dutch monopoly; cotton, coconut, maize and cinnamon followed, all worked by enslaved Africans.

sources.label: The French History of the Seychelles
History of Seychelles — French Settlement and Rule

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1771-spice-and-plantation-economy, claim TL:SYC:event:1771:spice-and-plantation-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capitulations during the Napoleonic Wars
claims.summary: Administrator Quéau de Quincy surrendered the islands to British squadrons several times, restoring French rule whenever they left.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1794-capitulations-during-the-napoleonic-wars, claim TL:SYC:event:1794:capitulations-during-the-napoleonic-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cession to Britain by the Treaty of Paris
claims.summary: Seychelles was formally ceded to Britain with Mauritius and governed thereafter as a dependency of Mauritius.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1814-cession-to-britain-by-the-treaty-of-paris, claim TL:SYC:event:1814:cession-to-britain-by-the-treaty-of-paris, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of slavery
claims.summary: Emancipation freed the several thousand enslaved Africans who formed the majority of the colony's population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1835-abolition-of-slavery, claim TL:SYC:event:1835:abolition-of-slavery, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberated Africans resettled
claims.summary: The Royal Navy landed thousands of Africans rescued from intercepted slave dhows, deepening the islands' Creole society.

sources.label: Seychelles at 250: Liberated slaves and the birth of the Creole identity

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1861-liberated-africans-resettled, claim TL:SYC:event:1861:liberated-africans-resettled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Separate Crown Colony
claims.summary: Seychelles was detached from Mauritius and constituted as a British Crown Colony in its own right.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1903-separate-crown-colony, claim TL:SYC:event:1903:separate-crown-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aldabra Atoll inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The raised coral atoll, home to the world's largest giant-tortoise population, was added to the World Heritage List for its outstanding natural value.

sources.label: Seychelles' Aldabra Atoll — decades as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1982-aldabra-atoll-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:SYC:event:1982:aldabra-atoll-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vallée de Mai inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: Praslin's palm forest, where the coco de mer grows wild, was recognised as a World Heritage Site for its unique flora.

sources.label: Vallée de Mai Nature Reserve — World Heritage List
Welcome to the Vallée de Mai

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1983-vallee-de-mai-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:SYC:event:1983:vallee-de-mai-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the United Kingdom
claims.summary: Seychelles became an independent republic within the Commonwealth, with James Mancham as first president and France-Albert René as prime minister.

sources.label: Seychelles (1976–present)
sources.publisher: University of Central Arkansas, DADM Project

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1976-independence-from-the-united-kingdom, claim TL:SYC:event:1976:independence-from-the-united-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup brings René to power
claims.summary: Supporters of France-Albert René overthrew Mancham in an almost bloodless coup while he was abroad; René took the presidency.

sources.label: Seychelles (1976–present)
sources.publisher: University of Central Arkansas, DADM Project

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1977-coup-brings-rene-to-power, claim TL:SYC:event:1977:coup-brings-rene-to-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: One-party socialist state
claims.summary: A new constitution made the Seychelles People's Progressive Front the sole legal party, with nationalisations and restrictions on the press.

sources.label: Seychelles (1976–present)
sources.publisher: University of Central Arkansas, DADM Project

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1979-one-party-socialist-state, claim TL:SYC:event:1979:one-party-socialist-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mike Hoare's mercenary raid fails
claims.summary: Mercenaries disguised as a beer-drinkers' club and backed from South Africa tried to seize power; the plot collapsed and they hijacked an airliner to flee.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1981-mike-hoare-s-mercenary-raid-fails, claim TL:SYC:event:1981:mike-hoare-s-mercenary-raid-fails, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to multiparty democracy
claims.summary: A new constitution restored multiparty politics; the first competitive presidential elections were held, won by René.

sources.label: Seychelles (1976–present)
sources.publisher: University of Central Arkansas, DADM Project

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-1993-return-to-multiparty-democracy, claim TL:SYC:event:1993:return-to-multiparty-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: High-income tourism and tuna economy
claims.summary: Tourism became the dominant sector and tuna fishing a leading export, lifting Seychelles to high-income status.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Seychelles: From empty islands to Creole republic", terralore.co/country/SYC/chronicle#ev-2015-high-income-tourism-and-tuna-economy, claim TL:SYC:event:2015:high-income-tourism-and-tuna-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
